result.instructions: Tools for Mercury, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "What is the current balance of each of our Mercury accounts?"; "Show me all transactions over $1,000 from the last 30 days."; "Which send-money requests are still waiting for approval?". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Mercury data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run mercury_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run mercury_request_feature to record the request. Paid plans: Pro (10,000 tool calls a month, $9/month or $90/year, for normal use) and Pro+ (100,000 tool calls a month, $39/month or $390/year, for automations and heavy use). A plan can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run mercury_upgrade without a plan: it returns both plans, each with a payment link for the user to open. mercury_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: mercury_request_send_money
tools.title: Request a payment (needs approval)
tools.description: Create a payment REQUEST from an account to a saved recipient. Mercury does not send the money now: the request waits for admin approval under the organization's approval policy. Only ACH, check and real-time payment are supported. Needs a Custom token with the RequestSendMoney scope. Reuse the same idempotency_key only to retry the same request. Mercury API: POST /account/{accountId}/request-send-money.

account_id.description: The source account id (from the matching list tool).

recipient_id.description: The recipient id (from the matching list tool).

amount.description: Amount in USD, a positive number with up to 2 decimals.

payment_method.description: How to pay. Wires are not supported here.

idempotency_key.description: A unique key you create for this request (for example a UUID). Reuse it only when you retry the same request.
